unresolved_warnings: The atom is conditional on exact compact-resolvent spectral completeness/multiplicity and therefore cannot by itself advance the existential Hilbert–Pólya bridge.
The endpoint exclusion is only for ordinary trace class; zeta/Dixmier/relative/distributional traces require separate definitions and convergence proofs rather than being rejected by this atom.
Zero counting contains no prime-power weights, so a trace formula can still fail prime matching even when its analytic trace notion is legitimate.
A noncompact or continuous-spectrum model can evade the compact-resolvent summability statement and must be analyzed in its own representation.
de Branges/canonical-system positivity can be RH-equivalent; it cannot be imported as an independent positivity certificate without a non-circularity audit.
de Bruijn–Newman flow and random-matrix phenomena are proposal/calibration signals only for this atom.
